question: Is Mount Jefferson's Whitewater Glacier route missing from the catalog, and what is its full row and trailhead coordinate?
answer: Confirmed missing: no Whitewater row exists in catalog-or-mountains.json under any spelling (or_mt_jefferson holds Center Ridge, Jefferson Park Glacier, North Ridge, North Milk Creek Glacier, South Ridge). It is the most popular route on the peak (Grade II, glacier plus class 4 summit pinnacle) and distinct from our Jefferson Park Glacier (different glacier, different trailhead side). Whitewater Trailhead is at the end of Road 2243 off Hwy 22 (about 7.5 mi of gravel), 4,140 ft. Fetched approach: Whitewater Trail 1.5 mi to Jefferson Park Trail, east 2.5 mi to the PCT, half a mile up into Jefferson Park, leave trail near pt 6166 up its ridge to a ~7,100 ft bench (moraine pond water), cross the crevassed Whitewater Glacier to the SE ridge at ~9,000 ft, 1,000 ft scree to Red Saddle, steep snow/ice traverse (pickets), then exposed scramble to the north ridge and a ~30 ft class 4 final pitch. About 8.5 mi and 6,500 ft gain one way per the fetched page.
recommendation: ADD route to or_mt_jefferson with the proposed row. Add Trailhead pin 44.70682,-121.87511 (fetched Oregon Hikers page coordinate). Attach tracks 3257845 / 2887420 to the new row only if they pass the usual track checks.

proposed.name: Whitewater Glacier
proposed.overview: The most popular line on Jefferson. From Jefferson Park you cross the moderately crevassed Whitewater Glacier to the southeast ridge, climb loose scree to Red Saddle, cross a steep snow-and-ice traverse where most parties place pickets, then finish up the airy summit pinnacle with about 30 feet of class 4 rock. Glacier gear and a rope are standard; allow a long day from a Jefferson Park camp.
proposed.approach: Drive the gravel Whitewater road to its end and hike the Whitewater and Jefferson Park trails to the Pacific Crest Trail, then up into Jefferson Park, roughly 4.5 miles. Leave the trail near the moraine and climb the ridge to a bench at about 7,100 ft, where the glacier begins. Wilderness permit required Jun 15-Oct 15.
proposed.descent_text: Reverse the route: downclimb or rappel the pinnacle, recross the Red Saddle traverse, then descend the scree to the southeast ridge and the glacier. Watch for rockfall above the traverse in afternoon heat.
